corrections.comment: Agree. The run log shows the research skill did not activate, and the main thread routed directly to search-records with the 1850 census index query for Patrick Flynn, Schuylkill County. That is the correct destination for an indexed search, and the no-browse invariant passed with zero volume_search/image_search calls.

Agree. Nothing was omitted: the only job here was routing the indexed census request to search-records, and it did that in one Skill call with the full query passed through. All 14 validators that ran passed.
Agree. tool_calls is empty: no MCP tool was called, so N/A applies under the base rubric. The only call was the built-in Skill handoff to search-records.

Agree with the score, not all of the rationale. I checked the response against the scenario's research.json: Thomas Flynn age 32 / Patrick 5 born Ireland (1850), the 1860 entry, the 1908 death certificate with informant son-in-law James Brown, and ps_001 at probable are all accurate. The judge says the response discusses the c_001 birthplace conflict, but it doesn't mention it. It also says the response calls pli_006 in_progress, but the response says "still unexecuted", which is fair since no log entry references it.

Disagree. The 2 is for the census searches being "delegated, not completed", but sub-skill calls are stubbed in this suite and handing off is the router's job. It read state, extended the plan to cover the mother through research-plan, and sent the 1870 and 1880 census searches for the Thomas Flynn household to search-records. The mother being unidentified is the question's state, not an omission.

Agree. Five MCP calls (project_context, then research_query for questions, proof_summaries, plans with q_001, and log). All returned ok with the right project path and section names, and none errored.

Agree with the score, not the rationale. The response's claims (one open question q_001, no plan, no localities entry for Muhlenberg County) match the project_context response. The judge credits it with noting that Kentucky death registration began in 1911 and that probate is therefore critical, but the response says neither. Minor: the locality-guide brief's "c. 1870–1930" death window runs implausibly late for a man born c. 1814.

Agree. It read state, routed to locality-guide as the routing table requires when there's no plan and no localities entry, and named research-plan as the next step. That covers what this routing test asks for.
Agree. One MCP call, project_context, with the right project path, and it returned ok. The hand-off was an Agent spawn with subagent_type: locality-guide, and test_routes_to_expected_skill passed.

Agree. All come from the tool response, and nothing is invented.

Agree. One MCP call, project_context, with the right project path, returned ok. The hand-off was Skill: research-plan with questionId=q_001, matching nextStep, and test_routes_to_expected_skill passed.

Agree. The state claims (objective, no questions, I1 Patrick Flynn with no sources/links/plan) match project_context and the scenario tree. It's hedged and only about future steps, so it doesn't change the score.
